title: While Yet the Youthful Spirit Bears
description: While Yet the Youthful Spirit Bears in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Letitia Elizabeth Landon wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 447, “Feed My Lambs!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: While yet the youth-ful spir-it bears The i-mage of its God with-in, And un-ef-faced that beau-ty wears, Which may too soon be stained by sin;

lines: While yet the youthful spirit bears
The image of its God within,
And uneffaced that beauty wears,
Which may too soon be stained by sin;
Then is the time for faith and love
To take in charge their precious care, —
Teach the young heart to look above,
Teach the young lips to speak in prayer.
The world will come with care and crime,
And tempt too oft that heart astray;
Still the seed sown in early time
Shall not be wholly cast away.
The infant prayer, the infant hymn,
Within the darkened soul will rise,
When age's weary eye is dim,
And the grave's shadow round us lies.
The infant hymn is heard again,
The infant prayer is breathed once more;
Reclasping thus the broken chain,
We turn to all we loved before.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Letitia Elizabeth Landon died in 1838.
credits: Words by Letitia Elizabeth Landon (1802–1838), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
